task: This is a synthetic newspaper-writing exercise using fictional reporting notes. Use only the supplied reporting notes. Write from the reporting snapshot as of September 8, 2026. Write a headline and a 450–650-word AP-style reported feature about Merrin Patterns' succession problem and what a small industrial workshop must preserve when it moves work from wooden patterns into digital files.

facts.text: An Aug. 4, 2026, workshop note records owner Ila Merrin checking a wooden pump-housing pattern against a paper drawing annotated with handwritten allowances.
Merrin Patterns makes patterns that foundries use to form molds for casting replacement pump parts and other industrial components.
The forms are not the finished metal parts; dimensions account for later casting and machining requirements.
Merrin, who opened the workshop in 1988, plans to reduce her working week from five days to three next year.
The business employs two assistants, including Toma Venn, who joined from a general machining job 18 months ago.
The workshop holds 120 active customer patterns and a separate shelf of retired patterns kept for reference.
Some customer agreements require permission before a pattern or drawing is supplied to an outside scanning service.
A pilot scanned 14 permitted patterns; ten could be used with existing written instructions and four needed further annotations.
The missing annotations concerned casting allowances and machining references, not simply the visible outside shape.
The pilot does not establish that every stored pattern can be reproduced accurately from a scan alone.
A quoted $18,000 digitization package includes first-year software access; renewal is quoted separately at $2,000 annually.
Customers have not agreed on how much of that cost they will pay through revised orders or storage fees.
Merrin said, "The shape can go into a file. The reason for that extra lip still needs to go with it."
Venn keeps a job notebook that links customer drawings to changes made after trial castings.
Venn said, "I am not learning a secret by watching once. I am learning which question to ask before cutting."
Foundry customer Keri Calden says reliable replacement patterns can matter more than speed when maintaining equipment whose original maker no longer supplies parts.
Calden has not committed to buying the pattern business or financing all its conversion costs.
Merrin says she intends to keep taking orders during the transition rather than announce a closing sale.
The workshop occupies two rooms behind a former agricultural dealership, with customer names painted on storage racks.
No completed sale, guaranteed successor or measured regionwide shortage of patternmakers is established by this reporting record.

forbidden_additions: A completed retirement sale or a guaranteed successor
All patterns can be copied from scans alone or the pilot proves a regionwide labor shortage
